- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.

- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area
- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

- Extend the native SM100/SM103 H96 DSA backward path to static Top-K widths 2049–2051, in both ordinary and deterministic modes.
- Add aligned, zero-filled 16-byte index staging for Top-K widths that are not multiples of four.
- Preserve the existing compact path and shared-memory layout for aligned Top-K widths.
- Add dispatch, numerical-gradient, and deterministic bitwise-repeatability coverage for Top-K 2048–2051.

## Why

With `kpool=4` DSA, selecting 2048 tokens can produce an effective Top-K width of 2048–2051 after including the current pooling-block tail.

The existing H96 dispatch only admitted selected aligned widths, so 2049–2051 fell back to the H64+H32 path.

Simply extending the dispatch whitelist is unsafe: these widths can produce unaligned row addresses and a partial final index vector for the existing 16-byte `cp.async` loader. This change aligns the source address down, stages one additional zero-filled vector when needed, and applies a logical prefix offset when consuming the indices.


## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

- No public API or signature changes.
- Native coverage is expanded only for contiguous BF16 H96, D576/V512 backward on supported SM100/SM103 devices.
- Top-K 2048 and other aligned shapes retain the existing staging specialization.
- Unsupported devices, layouts, data types, and head dimensions retain their existing fallback behavior.
- The unaligned specialization adds 32 bytes of shared memory; aligned shapes are unchanged.

## Testing

Environment:

- NVIDIA SM103
- CUDA 13.4 compiler
- cuDNN backend 9.20.0
- CuTe DSL 4.8.1
- PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130

Validation:

```bash
cd test/python

pytest -q -m L1 \
  deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_sparse_attention_backward.py::test_DSA_sparse_attention_backward_sm100_h96_d576_unaligned_topk_widths
# 8 passed

pytest -q -m L0 \
  deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_sparse_attention_backward.py \
  -k 'h96 or topk_stride_specialization'
# 31 passed, 355 deselected
```
The deterministic cases poison the output and workspace buffers, execute the kernel twice, and compare gradient storage bitwise.

Reference performance on the same SM103, comparing the official 1.32.0 fallback with this branch:

Top-K | Ordinary, 1.32.0 → PR | Deterministic, 1.32.0 → PR | Deterministic workspace
-- | -- | -- | --
2048 | 1.002 → 1.001 ms | 16.242 → 16.238 ms | 54 → 54 GiB
2049 | 1.501 → 1.152 ms | 25.953 → 16.412 ms | 72 → 54 GiB
2050 | 1.527 → 1.150 ms | 25.953 → 16.406 ms | 72 → 54 GiB
2051 | 1.473 → 1.152 ms | 25.953 → 16.397 ms | 72 → 54 GiB

- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area
- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

- Extend the native SM100/SM103 H96 DSA backward path to static Top-K widths 2049–2051, in both ordinary and deterministic modes.
- Add aligned, zero-filled 16-byte index staging for Top-K widths that are not multiples of four.
- Preserve the existing compact path and shared-memory layout for aligned Top-K widths.
- Add dispatch, numerical-gradient, and deterministic bitwise-repeatability coverage for Top-K 2048–2051.

## Why

With `kpool=4` DSA, selecting 2048 tokens can produce an effective Top-K width of 2048–2051 after including the current pooling-block tail.

The existing H96 dispatch only admitted selected aligned widths, so 2049–2051 fell back to the H64+H32 path.

Simply extending the dispatch whitelist is unsafe: these widths can produce unaligned row addresses and a partial final index vector for the existing 16-byte `cp.async` loader. This change aligns the source address down, stages one additional zero-filled vector when needed, and applies a logical prefix offset when consuming the indices.


## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

- No public API or signature changes.
- Native coverage is expanded only for contiguous BF16 H96, D576/V512 backward on supported SM100/SM103 devices.
- Top-K 2048 and other aligned shapes retain the existing staging specialization.
- Unsupported devices, layouts, data types, and head dimensions retain their existing fallback behavior.
- The unaligned specialization adds 32 bytes of shared memory; aligned shapes are unchanged.

## Testing

Environment:

- NVIDIA SM103
- CUDA 13.4 compiler
- cuDNN backend 9.20.0
- CuTe DSL 4.8.1
- PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130

pytest -q -m L1 \
